questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Please explain: *
Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: chose my study destination to combine strong expertise in ecology and biodiversity research with unique field opportunities in the Białowieża Forest. The Double Degree between the University of Copenhagen and the University of Warsaw offered both molecular and ecological perspectives, as well as valuable international experience.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It was a fantastic stay where I learned to work much more independently and take responsibility for projects. The field courses were excellent and very educational. The only reason I cannot give a top score is the enormous amount of administrative work it required. The University of Warsaw handled administration very well, but there was almost no support from KU, and we were often misinformed or instructed to do things incorrectly through the official administrative channels. We still haven’t received answers to some questions we asked KU more than four months ago.

questions.answer: We were quite well informed by Warsaw

Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: Course registration at the University of Warsaw was straightforward. Most courses were registered through the USOSweb system, and coordinators provided clear guidance on deadlines and procedures. For some field and laboratory courses, registration was done directly with the course coordinators by email, which worked smoothly. The only issue we had was that some courses that were offered in english changed after we started, and some courses were cancelled .

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Our Double degree coordinator as well as multiple professors helped us

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Quite succesful, but some were changed later which was unfortunate

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Coordinate well before applying to the courses and have backup classes you can take if things get changed

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The academic programme at the University of Warsaw was good. The courses were mostly well-structured, field-oriented, and provided a strong combination of practical and theoretical learning. The instructors were highly engaged and encouraged independent work and scientific discussion.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The courses were at a clear master’s level, requiring active participation, independent project work, and critical thinking. The workload and academic expectations matched or exeeded those at UCPH, and the field components provided valuable hands-on research experience.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: There were more focus on taxonomic knowledge than we have at UCPH. But overall a high level, just slightly diffrent focus.

What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: The University of Warsaw offered a wide range of cultural and social activities for students, including language courses, museum visits, and international student events organized by ESN. There were also hiking trips and nature excursions.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Join ESN events, its a great way to meet Polish students that want to engage with foreigners

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: I highly recommend visiting the Białowieża Forest, one of Europe’s last primeval forests and an unforgettable destination for anyone interested in nature and biodiversity. The Hel Peninsula and Gdańsk are perfect for coastal trips, with beautiful beaches and rich maritime history. Kraków offers stunning architecture and cultural heritage, and for hiking or skiing, the Tatra Mountains in southern Poland are absolutely worth a visit.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: t was okay, but quite different from Denmark, so it took some time to adjust. Once I got used to the pace and communication style, it became much easier and very rewarding.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Yes, talk to people in your classes and ask them for advice for what to do.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: The lack of smiling in public was hard at first, but the main challenge was that many people, even at the university, spoke only Polish, which made everyday communication more difficult at first. Combined with a more formal communication style, it took some time to adjust, but it became easier over time.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: People were very welcoming once you got to know them, and there was a genuine interest in nature, local traditions, and food. I also enjoyed how much outdoor life are part of the culture. Its just very diffrent to Denmark in a refreshing way.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Find someone at UCPH who is familiar with the administrative side of the Double Degree or Erasmus process otherwise, you may spend countless hours trying to solve issues on your own and risk delaying/losing SU payments.
Be proactive in communicating with both universities and keep written records of all correspondence.
Take advantage of the field courses and research opportunities they are incredibly rewarding and a great way to connect with both students and professors.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Join a lab group if possible and participate in conferences and fieldwork

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The most rewarding part of my exchange was the opportunity to work independently on real research projects and field courses, especially in the Białowieża Forest. It was incredibly valuable to conduct fieldwork for my master’s thesis in one of Europe’s last primeval forests, while gaining hands-on experience and building strong collaborations with researchers and students. Joining FUNDIVE was an amazing decision.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer:
The greatest challenge during my exchange was the lack of clear administrative support from the University of Copenhagen. Communication with the Outgoing Students office was often confusing, and I was repeatedly told that taking 45 ECTS was not possible within Erasmus, even though these 45 ECTS are part of my officially approved Double Degree programme with the University of Warsaw.

Several requests were delayed for weeks because staff were on vacation or unsure who had the authority to answer. Even now, my Online Learning Agreement still contains errors that have not been corrected despite multiple attempts to resolve them. The University of Warsaw, in contrast, handled all administrative matters efficiently and provided excellent support.
